mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-rates-4% periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims followed by a sustained decline in the monthly payrolls figure indicates weakening labor market strength, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in one month then UNRATE falls below 7% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained labor weakening indicators (Rank IC > 0.05 over 6 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer confidence accompanied by a concurrent decline in industrial production suggests conflicting demand signals that create uncertainty, driving down S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% while INDPRO falls by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both indicators are in conflict.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in the producer price index (PPI) above trend for two consecutive quarters is interpreted as supply-side inflation pressures that pre-empt equity valuation adjustments, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL quarterly acceleration > 0.5% above 5-year rolling average
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed inflation acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of the federal funds rate crosses above 5%, it reflects a tightening cycle that increases discount rates applied to future earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the prior 3 months of similar rate paths (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment accompanied by rising payrolls suggests a strong labor market that supports economic expansion, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for 4 consecutive months while PAYEMS rises by >2% monthly
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during moderate labor market periods (Rank IC < 0.03 over 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail sales followed by a sustained increase in building permits indicates shifting demand patterns that create uncertainty, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >8% in a month and UNRATE rises above 6% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) when the pattern recurs.

mechanism_narrative: During the late-cycle expansion regime characterized by rising industrial production and declining unemployment, the S&P 500 tends to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns regardless of short-term macro volatility.
candidate_trigger: regime: late-cycle expansion AND INDPRO rising AND UNRATE falling
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive in >80% of identified late-cycle expansion windows (empirical frequency).
